subject: VPC perimeter adjacency and control/data-plane routing readout
messages:
From: Samir Rao <acme-ops@acmecorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 09:14 -0800
Subject: Perimeter adjacency / control vs data-plane routing — need confirmation and runbook

Hi Vivek / Kim,

Thanks again for the runbook stub you shared last week. Before our staging cutover next month the network team needs a short, written readout confirming two things we flagged in onboarding:

1) Control-plane egress constraints — we need confirmation that the control plane (k8s/Redwood control API) only egresses to our management CIDRs and the Redundancy endpoints you listed, and that there are no unplanned egress paths to public IP ranges.
2) Data-plane adjacency and NAT/BGP expectations — we need the expected source IPs for inference traffic, whether NAT will be applied at the edge, and the BGP announcements we should see from the colo.

Can you provide a concise runbook excerpt (1–2 pages) and an annotated edge diagram? Please attach any ACL / iptables examples you recommend. I've attached our existing edge map for reference.

We also need to surface any pieces that will require changes on our side (firewall rules, route filters) so we can schedule work.

Appreciate a reply by EOD tomorrow if possible — we have a gating milestone on the 10th.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Senior Network Engineer, Acme Corp
acme-ops@acmecorp.com
Attachment: acme_vpc_edge_map.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <acme-ops@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 11:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Perimeter adjacency / control vs data-plane routing — need confirmation and runbook

Samir — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front, followed by next steps and attachments.

- Control-plane egress: Confirmed. Redwood's control plane for your private deployment will only egress to the three management endpoints in the attached runbook (management.redwood.net FQDNs resolving to our mgmt CIDRs), over TLS to the management NATs we provision. No other public egress will be used for control-plane communication.
- Data-plane adjacency / NAT / BGP: Data-plane (inference) originates from tenant NAT pools that are scoped to the tenant's edge cluster; by default we NAT to the edge public IP set we coordinate with you. For colo deployments where you prefer preserved source IPs we can operate with BGP-peered leafs (no NAT) — we documented both modes in the runbook. Expected BGP announcements are listed in the diagram notes.

Quick risks / notes:
- If you require strict source-IP preservation for telemetry, choose BGP-peered mode (we'll need your ASN and an agreed anycast route plan).
- If you prefer simpler firewall rules on your side, the default NATed pool is easier (single ASN announcement from Redwood edge).

I've attached a 2-page runbook excerpt (redwood_runbook_v0.9.md) and an annotated edge map (PDF) with the control/data demarc labeled. Irene — added you because of the cert rotation and KMS footprint mentioned below. Karthik — can you confirm the brief BGP blurb in INF-5432 matches the operational plan?

Next steps (proposed):
- We will update the runbook with your ASN & IP ranges (action: Acme).
- Schedule a 30-min handoff to walk the BGP/NAT options (action: Redwood — Vivek to propose times).
- Provide a small iptables/ACL snippet for both NATed and non-NAT modes (action: Kimberly — 1 business day).

Available times Thursday/Friday morning PST — I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_runbook_v0.9.md
Attachment: redwood_vpc_perimeter_annotated.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <acme-ops@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 13:18 -0800
Subject: Re: Perimeter adjacency / control vs data-plane routing — need confirmation and runbook

Samir — quick follow-up with the ACL snippets and diagram link. Inline excerpt from the runbook (iptables/NAT example):

- NATed mode (default edge NAT):
  * iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.240.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source <edge-public-ip-pool>
  * Expected egress: single announced /24 per edge pod (see diagram notes)

- BGP-peered mode (no-NAT):
  * Configure peer with ASN: 64512 (placeholder)
  * We expect your router to accept the prefix and preserve source IPs; Redwood will withdraw on failover.

Diagram (annotated): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqV-vpc-edge-diagrams — file: redwood_vpc_perimeter_annotated.pdf

I'll also paste the short checklist you'll want to run prior to staging cutover:
- Confirm ASN & permitted prefixes to be announced to Redwood
- Open management NAT CIDRs to TCP 443 outbound from control-plane hosts
- Provision BGP session(s) with hold timers we recommend in the runbook (30s/90s)

If you prefer, I can paste these exact ACL lines into your firewall change ticket.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Network Lead, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek / Kim — that is exactly the level we needed. A couple quick clarifications:

- For the NATed mode, can you confirm the edge-public-ip-pool will be a contiguous /24 per pod (we asked change window ops to expect /24s)?
- For BGP mode, our ASN is 65087 — I'll attach a signed contact and the list of permitted prefixes to INF-5432.
